observation.visible_scene: A wooden snap-trap apparatus sits on a textured dark mat in front of a reddish brick wall. The trap base holds a copper spring and a long U-shaped copper kill-bar. Resting on top of the bar is a smaller wooden lever tipped with a yellow clip, propped up at an angle by the wire loop. In the earliest frames a person's fingers are partly visible at the left edge of the frame.
visible_changes: The fingers at the left edge withdraw and leave the frame within the first several samples.
The small wooden lever with the yellow clip slowly rotates downward: its raised left end lowers progressively from a steep angle (early frames) to a near-horizontal position (late frames).
The copper kill-bar on the right side of the base gradually swings upward, changing from a roughly horizontal set position to a tall, near-vertical orientation by the end of the clip.
These two rotations proceed together in a slow, continuous manner; no sudden snap or impact is visible within the excerpt.
The brick background and mat texture remain unchanged throughout, with the trap base staying in the same position on the surface.
outside_clip_unknowns: What triggered or sustained the slow reconfiguration of the lever and kill-bar.
Whether the mechanism is being set, released, or merely relaxing.
What the hand at the left was doing before the clip began.
The final state of the trap after the last frame.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent downward tilt of the lever and upward swing of the bar are a single coupled motion or two independent slow movements.
Minor framing differences between samples (possible small camera shift versus object settling) cannot be resolved from the background alone.
The exact mechanical linkage between the small lever, the yellow clip, and the copper bar is not fully legible.
